result.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360$^{\circ}$ View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
result.summary: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360$^{\circ}$ scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed. We present PhotoGuider, a measure-then-frame method that answers both questions with compact learned scorers over one shared set of composition-aware features. The designed features are extracted using foundation and task-specific vision models and structured into four photographic tokens: Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, and Integrity. Our MLLM explainer is fine-tuned to generate composition-related explanations conditioned on images and measured token assessments. To our knowledge, PhotoGuider is the first method to combine explicit composition-based direction selection in 360$^{\circ}$ panoramas with refined framing, camera-parameter output for native re-rendering, and measurement-conditioned explanations. On two standard 2D cropping benchmarks, PhotoGuider achieves the highest average mIoU performance against ground-truth crops. In a blind ranking study, 120 participants ranked three cropping methods over 100 panoramic scenes from the public Poly Haven HDRI library, placing our framings first in 53.2% of cases, against 27.3% and 19.5% for two strong alternatives. Project page: https://ntuneillee.github.io/research/photoguider/

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PhotoGuider，用共享构图特征上的紧凑学习打分器先在 360° 全景中选出观看方向再做裁剪取景，并微调 MLLM 依据结构化的 Subject/Composition/Aesthetics/Integrity 四类「摄影 token」生成解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先测量再取景」的全景方向选择与 LVR 中决定看哪里的 LOOK 决策可能有概念联系，但这里是一次性打分而非迭代状态更新；MLLM 解释是否真正依赖测量 token 可供核查视觉信息使用与贡献分配问题。
